title: Spec changes
summary: What differs between the specs of two branches, by item and requirement.
description:
A line diff of the JSON files says which lines changed. This says what changed in the spec: which items and requirements were added, removed or reworded.

It compares a base (by default the default branch) with another branch or commit.

requirements.text: Items are matched by id. An item only one side has is added or removed; one that differs is changed; one that is the same isn't listed.
Requirements are matched by their id within the item. A reworded requirement shows its old and new text with the words that differ marked.
A requirement whose level or status changed shows the old and the new value. Leaving `level` out and writing `must` are the same.
Changes are listed in the outline's order, with removed items and requirements where they used to be.
A figure whose file changed shows the picture from both sides. A changed caption alone doesn't.
A summary counts the added, changed and removed items and requirements.
A pull request that touches `.spec` links to the changes between its base branch and its head commit.
A side without a spec counts as an empty one: everything on the other side is added or removed.
Each changed item opens in the spec browser, on the side that has it.

questions: Should a requirement that moved to another item be shown as moved rather than removed and added?
